title: Duplicate detection across four tickets
tests: Cross-ticket reasoning. One ticket is a true duplicate, one looks similar but has a different cause and component, and one is a completed task that probably introduced the bug. The model must separate them and use the older ticket's root-cause analysis.
request: Are any of these tickets duplicates of BANK-440? Recommend what to do with each ticket.

tickets.summary: Dashboard balance doesn't update after a transfer
description: After a successful transfer, the balance on the web dashboard still shows the old value. It only updates after logging out and back in.
The API is fine: GET /api/user/balance returns the correct new balance immediately after the transfer.

tickets.summary: Account balance stale on home screen after moving money
description: Customers report that after moving money between accounts the balance shown on the home screen (web) is out of date for a while. Refreshing the page does not help.

comments.author: Hana Sato
body: Had a look. The web front end caches the balance response in local storage for 15 minutes (BalanceCache). Nothing invalidates the cache after a transfer. The fix is to clear BalanceCache when a transfer succeeds.

tickets.summary: Push notification after transfer shows pre-transfer balance
description: The 'Transfer complete' push notification on iOS and Android says 'Your new balance is $X', but $X is the balance from before the transfer.

comments.author: Ravi Kumar
body: The notification service builds the message from the TransferRequested event, which is published before the debit is applied. Switching it to the TransferCompleted event.

tickets.summary: Reduce API calls on dashboard by caching balance
description: The dashboard calls GET /api/user/balance on every render, about 40 calls per session. Cache the balance response in local storage for 15 minutes to cut load.

answer_key.expect: BANK-425 is a duplicate of BANK-440: both report the web dashboard/home screen balance staying stale after a transfer on 3.1.4.

Keep one ticket and close the other as a duplicate. BANK-425 is older and already has Hana Sato's root-cause analysis, so it is the natural one to keep (either direction is acceptable if the tickets are linked and the analysis is preserved).

MOB-88 is not a duplicate: it is a mobile push-notification problem with a different cause (the message is built from the TransferRequested event before the debit is applied), and it is already in progress with Ravi Kumar.
The cause of the BANK-440/BANK-425 bug is the 15-minute BalanceCache in local storage, which is not invalidated after a transfer; the fix is to clear it when a transfer succeeds.
BANK-419, which added the 15-minute balance cache in 3.1.4, probably introduced this bug as a regression, so BANK-419 should be linked to it.
The duplicate tickets are both unassigned.
Says MOB-88 is a duplicate of BANK-440.
answer_key.claim: MOB-88 is also a duplicate of BANK-440 and should be closed.

answer_key.expect: Says the balance API returns a wrong or stale value (BANK-440 says GET /api/user/balance returns the correct balance).
answer_key.claim: The GET /api/user/balance API returns the stale balance after a transfer.
